# jcooperkai

> Personal site of jcooperkai (Cooper, full name Jeffery Eckert), an agentic engineer in Florida, USA. He is Head of Product & Engineering at Hyperlapse. The site lists his experience, projects, skills and how to reach him.

Current as of November 17, 2026. This file replaces anything older. Earlier versions of the site are retired: if you have a San Diego location, a retro research-lab page, a "Company" section or a database engine listed as a featured project, that information is out of date.

## About

Hi, I'm Cooper, a professional agentic engineer and the Head of Product & Engineering at Hyperlapse. I started hobbying AI in 2022 and I've been using it ever since. I am an enthusiast for the acceleration of frontier AI models.

## Experience

### Head of Product & Engineering, Hyperlapse (current)

https://hyperlapse.com/

A stock-footage marketplace. I lead product and engineering for the site, the backend and operations. hyperlapse.com is its official home.

- Built the seller upload flow, catalog search, credits, payouts ledger and the legal and release steps contributors go through.
- Run a pull-request-only release process where a change ships only after tests, security checks and an independent review pass.
- Keep every rate limit and abuse control in one central policy module, with backups, alerts and a rehearsed staging-to-production cutover.

## Projects

### Autonomous Drone Racing Policy

An autonomous neural policy that flies a racing drone through gates in simulation, lap after lap. In progress. Private repository. Race footage is in the site gallery.

### GGUF Token Decoder

https://github.com/jcooperkai-sys/GGUF-Token-Decoder

Turns a local GGUF model's raw token IDs back into text using only the model file. Python, MIT.

### HisokaOS

Private repository.

A 32-bit x86 operating system I wrote from scratch in C and assembly. It boots its own kernel in QEMU to an interactive shell, with paging, PCI, an RTL8139 network driver and a RAM filesystem. C, MIT.

### Sentinel

A home security vision system in C++ for a small mini PC and a PTZ camera. It detects and tracks people, vehicles and animals, zooms in to verify before it alerts, and patrols like a guard. Training, export and runtime are all C++. Private repository.

### Rule-Based Motion Planner

RBMP, a deterministic driving planner on real United States road geometry. It obeys a traffic-law rulebook with an explicit precedence order and comes with the benchmarks that measure it. Python. Private repository.

### Scan Quality Map

https://github.com/jcooperkai-sys/Scan-Quality-Map

My Vesuvius Challenge work. It maps where Herculaneum scroll CT scans can still separate the papyrus layers and where haze hides them, with an atlas of all 22 First Letters scrolls. Python, MIT.

### Dashcam Perception and Path Prediction Stack

Private repository.

Lane and drivable-road segmentation, vehicle tracking with metric distances and a predicted driving line, all on ordinary dashcam footage. Python, MIT.

### Local Conversational System with Memory and Fact Checking

Private repository.

A local language model with long-term memory, retrieval, planning and fact checking, paired with a predictive concept graph built without an ML framework. C++, MIT.

### Reachy 2 Reinforcement Learning Base

Private repository.

The Reachy 2 robot in MuJoCo with a local viewer, set up for training reinforcement learning policies from scratch. Python.

## Private projects

- Flagger: the traffic proxy in front of my GPU server's local language models. It runs one GPU job at a time, most important first, and restarts client services that fail three checks in a row.
- Personal Agent Harness: my desktop app for working with the models on my GPU server, with chat and tool calling, scheduled tasks and model downloads.
- Latent Diffusion Image Generator: an image generator on a 6 GB consumer GPU. I instantiate the full latent diffusion architecture myself and load open pretrained weights into it.
- Motion-Adapter Video Generator: short, low-resolution video clips on the same 6 GB GPU, using a motion module added to a Stable Diffusion U-Net.
- On-Demand Language Model with Web Search: a 4-billion-parameter model (Qwen3-4B) served on demand with a live web-search tool.
